hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: We must remove n // 2 elements from nums1 and n // 2 elements from nums2.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Find the distinct elements unique to nums1, unique to nums2, and common to both.

hints.title: Algorithmic Steps
hints.text: Greedily keep up to n // 2 unique elements from each array first, then fill any remaining quota with common elements.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumSetSize(self, nums1: list[int], nums2: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums1)
        s1 = set(nums1)
        s2 = set(nums2)
        common = s1 & s2
        u1 = len(s1 - common)
        u2 = len(s2 - common)
        take1 = min(u1, n // 2)
        take2 = min(u2, n // 2)
        rem1 = n // 2 - take1
        rem2 = n // 2 - take2
        take_common = min(len(common), rem1 + rem2)
        return take1 + take2 + take_common
```

variables: n: length of each input array
complexity.notes: Hash set intersections and greedy allocation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute force combinations of n/2 removals is exponential.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use set difference and intersection to partition items into disjoint categories.
